svg.text: KST — PD BENCH SUPPLY 5 / 9 / 12 / 15 / 20V · Wiring diagram (2D mockup)
KenhSangTao.COM · PD 100W source (wall charger OR power bank) · CMTPD trigger board (auto-cycling) · ESP32-C3 Super Mini · INA226 (R010 shunt) · OLED 0.96" · SY8205 buck-boost · 1× 2N7000 (Q1)
INA226 — measures V / A / W (R010 shunt = 0.01Ω)

g.text: short = next level · hold = back to min

svg.text: beeps on power-up + every level change

g.text: MARKED FACE toward you · pins pointing down
1. COMMON GND — tie everything to one point: trigger board, SY8205, ESP32, INA226, OLED, both output posts.
2. INA226: swap shunt R100 → R010 (0.01Ω); tie VBS ↔ IN−. ESP32 draws power at node (A), BEFORE the shunt ⇒ displayed current = real LOAD current.
3. Trigger board AUTO-CYCLES (5→9→12→15→20→5…) ⇒ ONLY Q1 needed → the 2 KEY-button pins (D to KEY, S to GND). Gate: 100Ω in series + 100k to GND.
4. Leave ALL config pads OPEN: S1 (key lock), F1 (Run to LOW), F2 (Run to TOP), F1+F2 (Run Cycle), PD ONLY, DM/DP. Only solder wires to the + / − pads.
5. SY8205 jumpered to 5V. Test first: feed 5.0V into IN+ with a ~200mA load, measure OUT. Can't hold 5V → power ESP32 from a separate 5V, or set ALLOW_5V=false.
6. Place the 1000µF + 100nF caps RIGHT AT the ESP32 5V/GND pins.
7. Both OLED & INA226 have onboard I2C pull-ups; if I2C is flaky, remove the pull-ups on one module.
8. Use ≥ 20AWG for red (power) & black (GND) wires — 100W at 20V = 5A.
9. 2-pin active buzzer (has its own driver): + → GPIO21, − → GND. Beeps on power-up and on every level change.
